questions.q: Antonio Toledo is most famous for designing which iconic building in Manila, known for its hexagonal tower and clock?
questions.n: Toledo designed this landmark, which is famous for its unique layout that resembles a coffin from an aerial view.

questions.q: Toledo collaborated with Juan Arellano on the design of the Legislative Building. What is this building known as today?
o: The National Museum of Fine Arts
The Cultural Center of the Philippines
The Supreme Court of the Philippines
The National Library of the Philippines
questions.n: This grand neoclassical structure, originally intended to be a library then a senate building, is a Toledo-Arellano collaboration.

questions.q: Which provincial capitol building, considered one of the most beautiful in the country, was designed by Antonio Toledo?
questions.n: Toledo designed this neoclassical gem in Tacloban, which served as the seat of the Commonwealth Government for a time.

questions.q: Toledo's architectural style is strictly defined by which movement, emphasizing order, symmetry, and classical Greek/Roman elements?
questions.n: His career at the Bureau of Public Works was defined by the grand, formal language of the Neoclassical style.

questions.q: True or False: Antonio Toledo was the youngest among the first group of Filipino pensionado architects sent to the United States.
questions.n: Toledo was indeed the youngest of the early pensionado architects, outliving many of his peers and serving long in the government.
